#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

# Refuse to run against a server that is not ours: an app left running on $PORT (an earlier
# bin/start that was never stopped, another sandbox) would take the tests and fail them all.
if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "bin/e2e: something is already serving on port ${PORT}; stop it (bin/stop) or set PORT to a free port" >&2
  exit 2
fi

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL. A loaded
# machine can take minutes to bring the JVM up; running the specs before it is ready fails every
# one of them for no reason, so wait long and fail loudly rather than run against nothing.
ready=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" != 1 ]; then
  echo "bin/e2e: the app did not become healthy on port ${PORT} within 300s; see .run/app.log" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

content.text:
I made no changes, because the app already does what the request asks. I ran `bin/e2e` against the code as I found it, and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` passed: the main "preview exports" test and scenarios 1–3.

The main test checks the case the request describes: a claim due 10.00 exports as 10.00, exports as 11.00 in both the people and claims CSVs once the preview is set to 2026-05-01, and goes back to 10.00 once the preview is cleared.

It already works because of how preview is built:
- **Front end:** while a preview date is set, `previewInterceptor` (`src/main/frontend/src/app/core/preview.ts`) adds an `X-Preview` header to every request to a sheet.
- **Server:** for a read carrying that header, `PreviewGuard` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/asof/PreviewGuard.java`) sets the sheet's today to the preview date inside a transaction it rolls back afterwards, so nothing is stored.
- **Exports:** the four exports (people, claims, statement and pools) all re-read the sheet from the server just before building the CSV. Those re-reads carry the header, and the people, claims and statement exports work out dues using the preview date, so they come out at preview figures.

I also checked the other places that use the sheet's real today rather than the preview date: defer, generating periods, plan start and the "Today" shown on screen. Those are changes or real-date displays, and the existing design says changes always use the real today, so I left them alone.

The test only covers the people and claims exports. The statement and pools exports re-read the sheet the same way, but no test exercises them.
